Still, Chanana believes a broader crackdown is not inevitable, as Washington may choose to balance national security concerns against the costs to American tech firms and innovation.

However, Fahy of Capital Economics said the new measures underscore how hawkish the mood in Washington has become.

“Congress has long favoured a tougher approach to China, but US President Donald Trump has so far appeared more willing to compromise. The fact that these new restrictions have been introduced by the administration, rather than imposed by Congress, suggests this distinction is narrowing.”

This situation leaves the already-fragile US-China relationship on even shakier footing, with a senior White House official reportedly claiming that US export controls would not be up for negotiation at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings in China from Nov 17 to 19.

Beijing has already condemned the restrictions and said it will “take the necessary steps to safeguard its legitimate interests”.

Fahy said: “The first of those steps may be to appeal directly to Trump in Shenzhen. The second could be retaliation – for example, a tightening of critical mineral export controls. If that happens, the existing trade truce will have all but broken down.”

A day after the US announced new chip restrictions, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said the Government could facilitate checks by the US on companies in the Republic to address any concerns over how advanced semiconductor chips are deployed.

While Singapore does not enforce the export controls of other countries, it will take “clear and firm” action against businesses that use the city-state to circumvent them or breach its laws, he added.

“We want to uphold the rule of law, and we want to uphold Singapore’s reputation as a trusted business hub,” he said on Nov 17, when asked about the issue during an interview with Singapore media after the ASEAN Summit in Manila.

data.title: Malaysia says growth stronger than expected but AI risks loom
data.description:
KUALA LUMPUR – Malaysia’s economy expanded faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, supported by demand for artificial intelligence and resilient domestic spending, as officials said they are trying to gauge the impact of new US rules on AI.

Gross domestic product rose 5.5% in the three months through September, more than the statistics department’s 5.3% advance estimate.

Economists expected no revision.

Growth surged to 6.9% in September, Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) said in a statement.

“The Malaysian economy is well-positioned to build on its momentum in 2027,” governor Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said at a briefing on Nov 18, predicting growth of more than 5% in 2026.

“Downside risks include re-escalation of conflict in the Middle East and lower-than-expected commodity production.”

Another downside risk is if AI returns disappoint, Rasheed said, though he predicted the tech upcycle “will be sustained into next year, although at a moderate level compared to what we’ve seen”.

Malaysia’s status as a net energy exporter has allowed it to maintain some of the world’s lowest fuel costs despite the Iran war, shielding it from the high energy prices that have battered neighbours such as Thailand and the Philippines.

But the data underscores its reliance on the AI boom, just as the US examines whether South-east Asian countries are allowing China access to advanced AI chips and servers.

Data centre operators in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil will need a US government licence to purchase advanced AI chips from Nvidia and other American manufacturers, according to an interim rule released on Nov 16 by the US Commerce Department.

The measure seeks to restrict China and other US adversaries from accessing offshore computing power that uses US-designed processors.

“This is an example of the geopolitics that we are all facing,” Rasheed said, noting it is too early to know the impact of the rule change.

“In terms of the impact on data centre investment, based on our estimates of the ongoing and planned projects, it is expected to remain strong up to 2028,” he added.

Out of the 120 companies in data centres, China accounts for only 13%, according to Rasheed, with the US, Australia and domestic interests accounting for the rest. 

It was unclear what Rasheed’s statistics referred to.

US hyperscalers account for the bulk of announced investment in Malaysia, while more than half of data centre capacity is in co-location facilities, where Chinese workloads may rival or exceed American ones, according to a report on Nov 18 from Gareth Leather, Capital Economics’ senior Asia economist in London. 

“The restrictions could affect a much larger share of Malaysia’s data centre industry than ownership figures suggest,” Leather wrote. “Any resulting slowdown in investment would add to the drag from an anticipated cooling in the global AI investment cycle.”

While the quarterly expansion was slower than the second-quarter pace of 6%, growth accelerated to 6.9% in September.

Rasheed noted the country’s businesses have adapted to supply disruptions even as they face higher costs. 

Firms remained optimistic on the outlook well into 2027, the central bank said, citing business expansion, tourism activities, electronics demand and commodity prices.

Rasheed said electrical and electronic firms’ order books have been solid, showing strong demand.

The ringgit extended an earlier decline, weakening 0.6% against the dollar and underperforming other Asian currencies on Nov 18.

Kuala Lumpur’s benchmark stock index held earlier losses, declining 0.3%.

The third-quarter growth “is bang in line with our forecast and shows not just remarkable resilience, but also the economy powering through multiple external shocks”, said Nomura Holdings economist Euben Paracuelles.

“There is no need for the monetary stance to remain accommodative when growth is above potential for several quarters in a row, and pipeline price pressures are building.” 

BNM is set to raise its benchmark rate by 25 basis points in the first quarter, Paracuelles added.

The central bank kept interest rates unchanged at 2.75% at its final policy meeting of 2026 earlier in November, but signalled it would be ready to act if price pressures grow.

The ringgit has declined around 1% against the dollar in 2026, compared with declines of more than 6% for the Indonesian, Philippine and Thai currencies, limiting the impact of imported inflation.

The ringgit held a 0.4% drop from earlier in the day against the dollar, underperforming other currencies in Asia on Nov 18.

Kuala Lumpur’s benchmark stock index held earlier losses, declining 0.3%.

“Exchange rate movements are expected to remain primarily influenced by external developments,” BNM said.

It will “closely monitor global developments and remains committed to ensuring the orderly functioning of the domestic foreign exchange market”.

Malaysia’s economy grew 5.6% in the first three quarters of 2026, well above the government’s revised growth forecast of 4.8% to 5.3% for the year.

The government in October raised the forecast from 4% to 5% previously.

Household spending remains firm, as fuel subsidies helped shield consumers from elevated energy costs.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in October also announced more cash aid and a higher minimum wage for 2027 to ease cost-of-living pressures.

Inflation is set to “trend higher but remain contained” in 2026 and 2027, BNM said on Nov 18.
BLOOMBERG

data.title: Alibaba’s AI ambitions face steep challenge in US chip controls
data.description:
Alibaba Group Holding is facing mounting pressure to show it can deliver on its artificial intelligence business plan despite new limits on its access to data centre chips.

Its Hong Kong-listed shares capped a nine-day losing streak ahead of results due later on Nov 19 from the internet firm. Alibaba’s market value stands at US$216 billion (S$278.43 billion), less than half its level just over a year ago when investors were betting on it to lead China’s AI industry.

Draft US rules announced on Nov 16 would close a key workaround for Chinese hyperscalers to use advanced chips. That is making analysts turn more cautious on Chinese AI companies’ cloud growth potential as well as their ability to train and run next-generation models.

“For Alibaba, they depend heavily on access to computing power, so this will be an important setback,” said Matt Maley, chief market strategist at Miller Tabak.

“It’s likely going to create a situation where it will take longer for them to build an ecosystem that can compete with the most advanced American technology.”

The new US rules are aimed at preventing Chinese firms from renting cutting-edge chips at data centres abroad.

Alibaba and its peers are already banned from direct buying the most advanced processors, and Nvidia said this week it is no longer shipping lower-end Hopper data centre chips to China as well.

Part of Alibaba’s ambition to build 20GW of data centre capacity before 2032 depends on expansion across regions like South-east Asia. Chips made in-house by its T-Head unit may provide some buffer, but still trail the performance of Nvidia’s top products.

Fresh challenges aside, Alibaba’s results are expected to show a continued drag on its e-commerce business from sluggish Chinese consumption and tough competition.

Focus will be on whether that can be offset by its fast-growing cloud operation, which accounted for 18% of total revenue in the June quarter.

Among its peers, Tencent Holdings posted results after a Nov 18 close showing a negative profit impact from heavy AI spending. The company also warned that Washington curbs on Chinese access to overseas data centres will hamper development of its next AI model.

Nevertheless, JPMorgan Chase & Co analysts including Alex Yao expect US regulations to hurt Alibaba less than firms more directly exposed like MiniMax Group.

“The rule covers China-headquartered cloud providers operating abroad, but we estimate AliCloud’s overseas AI revenue at below 10% of its cloud revenue, so the direct revenue impact is small,” they wrote in a note, maintaining overweight on Alibaba.

The bullish case is also bolstered by valuations, with the stock trading at about 10 times to forward earnings estimates. That is down from its three-year average of nearly 13 times and similar to current multiples for Tencent and Baidu.

Nomura Holdings analysts including Jialong Shi are cautious on the impact of the new regulations overall, though they see leading hyperscalers holding up better.

“Independent AI labs, perhaps with the exception of DeepSeek, could face greater challenges in securing advanced Nvidia GPU capacity to train their next-generation models,” they wrote in a note on Nov 17.

“Comparatively, Alibaba and ByteDance might be better positioned, in our view supported by their existing GPU resources and greater financial capabilities.” BLOOMBERG

data.title: Nvidia tells employees that company is moving on from Jensen Huang era
data.description:
SANTA CLARA - At a town-hall meeting with employees on Nov 18, Nvidia’s interim Chief Executive Officer Colette Kress reiterated her confidence in the company after the ouster of longtime leader Jensen Huang.

“We’ve got this,” she told staff, repeating a phrase she used during the company’s earnings call the day before, according to a person who attended. The chipmaker, facing external campaigns to reinstate Huang, also made it clear that the co-founder and CEO won’t be coming back.

The meeting marked a new chapter for a company seeking to rebound from upheaval and scandal. Huang, who ran Nvidia for more than 30 years and built it into an AI powerhouse, left last week under the cloud of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who the US government has suspected of spying for China.

Flanked by more than 30 board members and senior executives, Kress touted the company’s recent financial results, thanking employees for their efforts in what she called a “great quarter”. On Nov 17, the company topped analysts’ estimates with its sales and earnings and boosted its revenue forecast for the next fiscal year.

Nvidia co-founder Chris Malachowsky spoke to the audience about the company’s core values, encouraging staff to remain intellectually honest and direct. 

The chipmaker’s roughly 47,300 employees are facing a future without the only CEO Nvidia has ever had. Under his leadership, they built a technology pioneer that’s central to the AI revolution. On Nov 18, Kress called them brilliant minds and said the mission would remain the same. 

Some current and former employees, as well as Silicon Valley figures close to Huang, are still supporting the old CEO and calling for his return. But the board has dismissed the idea.

The meeting ended with the Tom Petty and The Heartbreakers’ song I Won’t Back Down. BLOOMBERG

data.title: GTA VI frenzy spotlights potential insurance risks lurking in digital infrastructure
data.description:
Millions of gamers around the world have logged on for the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, arguably the century’s most anticipated video game, offering a glimpse of the vast, interconnected digital infrastructure the global economy increasingly relies on.

No major disruption is expected from the rollout. But the scale of demand around one of the gaming industry’s biggest releases underscores a broader risk for insurers: a failure at a shared cloud, payments or technology provider could affect thousands of businesses at once.

After 13 years in development and an estimated US$1 billion (S$1.29 billion) or more in production costs, Grand Theft Auto VI began rolling out globally on Nov 19, drawing the kind of attention that few entertainment releases ever command.

But the fervour also underscores how much modern businesses depend on the digital infrastructure that makes such mass online activity possible, and the risks insurers face when that infrastructure fails.

“A launch of the scale of GTA VI is effectively a built-in stress test of the shared digital economy infrastructure,” said Marcos Alvarez, managing director at Morningstar DBRS.

Insurers cover businesses against financial losses stemming from disruptions to their operations, including some caused by technology failures.

As companies increasingly rely on the same cloud providers, payment systems and digital platforms, a single outage could trigger claims from multiple policyholders at once, amplifying exposure.

Despite the frenzy surrounding the launch, any disruption on launch day or in the days that follow would not necessarily spell disaster for insurers, industry experts said.

“The recent technology outages have been a case in point with the gap between the economic cost and the actual insured loss being quite large due to policy limits, retentions, waiting periods, and coverage exclusions,” Alvarez added.

Business interruption could be a major source of claims, but coverage could also extend to costs associated with data recovery, system restoration, cyberattacks and outages at third-party technology providers, depending on the policy.

“This is an area that is evolving rapidly for the insurance industry. Insurers are refining how they assess, model and manage these interconnected exposures,” said Loretta Worters, a spokesperson for the Insurance Information Institute.

“That means looking beyond an individual company’s cybersecurity protections to understand its reliance on third-party providers, the concentration of those dependencies across their portfolios and the potential for a single event to generate losses across multiple policyholders.” REUTERS

data.title: Anthropic IPO raises US$81.3 billion to top SpaceX’s record debut
data.description:
Anthropic PBC and its seven co-founders have raised US$81.3 billion (S$104.81 billion) in an upsized IPO, becoming the first frontier AI lab tapping the public markets to fund its development of thinking machines.

The artificial intelligence firm sold 956.4 million shares and the co-founders sold 23.6 million shares for US$83 each, according to a statement on Nov 18, above the marketed range. The company had marketed 801.4 million shares, while the co-founders offered 23.6 million shares, in a range of US$70 to US$78 each, according to its filings.

Pricing the shares above the range gives the company a fully diluted valuation of roughly US$1.5 trillion.

The IPO is the biggest of all time, topping SpaceX’s US$75 billion base deal. Including a US$26 billion private placement listed in Anthropic’s filings, the offering as a whole would raise US$107.3 billion, lifting it above SpaceX’s total of US$86.2 billion including its so-called over-allotment option.

Anthropic’s debut marks a watershed moment for AI, signalling that investors have begun to expand their focus from primarily backing chipmakers and other infrastructure providers to the makers of platforms such as Claude, as they weave themselves into the fabric of business, academia, government and healthcare.

Soaring demand

Demand for the IPO soared, nearing seven times the number of orders for the shares available, Bloomberg News reported on Nov 15. Buyers from Wall Street to London to Tokyo clamoured for a slice of a stock that is expected to quickly join indexes such as the Nasdaq 100 after it begins trading on Nov 19.

Bankers told prospective investors that existing backers would be prioritised by Anthropic, and some would-be buyers would receive smaller allocations than they expect, people familiar with the matter have said.

Some investors are offering a portion of their Anthropic IPO allocation to other prospective backers, letting them collect additional fees and reduce their risk before trading begins, while others with pre-IPO stakes are marketing them to buyers via special purpose vehicles.

At a roughly US$1.5 trillion valuation, Anthropic would join the 15 largest publicly traded companies, neck and neck with Tesla but ahead of Eli Lilly & Co, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

The valuation is below the US$2 trillion floated months ago, but well above US$1.1 trillion that some on Wall Street suggested in the depths of the recent sell-off in tech stocks.

Anthropic’s listing is the first by a frontier AI lab, a cohort of firms building the most advanced models that are intended to tackle difficult problems and assist users in complex tasks such as software design, legal work and scientific discovery. The debut puts the company firmly ahead of rival OpenAI, which is not planning to go public before 2027.

The stock market did not offer a supportive setting for the Claude chatbot maker’s debut, with the Nasdaq 100 Index down 4.4% over the past week until closing on Nov 18.

Nvidia extended a losing streak to a fifth day, sinking 2.9% during regular trading, a day after the chipmaker reported earnings that beat expectations. It is set to buy US$10 billion of Anthropic stock as part of the private placement, the filings show.

“We’re not super fussed on when exactly, what month or what day, or what market conditions we go public into,” Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei, told JPMorgan Chase & Co CEO Jamie Dimon at an event on Nov 13. He said the best piece of advice he has received throughout the process is: “Never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it’s really worth.”

The debut is set to enhance the personal fortunes of the co-founders, including Amodei, as well as many of Anthropic’s employees. It will also juice returns for its venture capital backers, including Iconiq, Coatue Management and Spark Capital, which has a seat on the board.

Goldman Sachs Group and Morgan Stanley led Anthropic’s IPO, with participation from 20 other banks, the filing shows. The stock is expected to trade on Nov 19 on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT. BLOOMBERG

data.title: Tencent says new US chip curbs won’t hurt cloud revenue, may slow model training
data.description:
BEIJING – China’s Tencent Holdings said on Nov 18 that new US restrictions on remote access to advanced AI chips would not substantially hurt its cloud revenue, though they would likely slow development of its next AI model.

Washington this week unveiled rules restricting remote access to advanced US AI chips through overseas data centres.

Shares in Chinese cloud service providers, including Tencent, fell on Nov 17 after the announcement.

“We actually don’t see an impact, because our cloud business today is primarily running inference,” chief strategy officer James Mitchell told analysts on a post-earnings call.

Mitchell said Tencent’s more efficient models could now be run on a “surprisingly limited number” of domestic chips.

“We think that our cloud revenue will not be substantially adversely affected by the changes,” he said.

President Martin Lau called the tighter restrictions “unfortunate” and said they left Chinese companies with less advanced computing power.

Lau said the measures would affect AI model training and likely slow development of Tencent’s next model in the near term.

Over the longer run, Chinese companies would have to rely on domestic supply chains and chips, he said, adding that the latest restrictions were likely to accelerate their development.

Missing expectations

The comments came after Tencent reported 8% growth in third-quarter revenue on Nov 18, missing expectations and slowing from the previous quarter as momentum in its gaming business cooled.

Demand for artificial intelligence services continued to boost Tencent’s cloud business, a key focus for investors assessing whether the company’s heavy AI spending is beginning to generate returns.

The tech giant reported revenue of 207.3 billion yuan (S$40.1 billion) for the three months ended September, below an LSEG consensus estimate of 210.8 billion yuan. Revenue grew 11% in the previous quarter.

Revenue from fintech and business services, which includes the cloud unit, rose 9% to 63.7 billion yuan, with demand for AI-related cloud services a key driver.

Chinese technology companies have struggled to secure advanced Nvidia chips because of longstanding US export restrictions, leaving them at a disadvantage to some US rivals.

Tencent said in 2025 that chip shortages were constraining cloud growth as it prioritised using AI chips internally over renting computing power to external clients.

Revenue from value-added services, which includes gaming, rose 3% to 98.3 billion yuan in the quarter.

Domestic gaming revenue increased 11%, while international gaming revenue slid 9%.

Net profit rose 0.8% to 63.61 billion yuan, beating analysts’ expectations of 59.46 billion yuan.

Capital expenditure totalled 81.4 billion yuan in the September quarter, up from 52.8 billion yuan in the June quarter.

Tencent spent 84.7 billion yuan in the first half of 2026, exceeding the roughly 79 billion yuan it spent in all of 2025. REUTERS

data.title: Easier QR code payments, smoother online checkouts to come with enhanced PayNow
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Consumers can look forward to easier QR code payments here and a smoother online shopping checkout process as enhancements to the PayNow instant payments system are rolled out progressively from 2027.

Tourists visiting Singapore and Singaporeans travelling overseas can also expect more payment options as links between local and regional QR payment networks are expanded through the enhanced SGQR+.

These proposed enhancements and their implementation road map were outlined in the PayNow Generation 2 Phase 2 report released by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) on Nov 18.

The first phase examined how PayNow has evolved since its 2017 launch, with findings released in June. The second phase has identified seven enhancements to address gaps identified in the review, to be made between 2027 and 2028.

Through the enhanced SGQR+, Singaporeans and tourists will be able to pay with their preferred apps without having to check which QR schemes are accepted by the merchant, as Singapore connects to more major regional QR networks through SGQR+.

This will also enable more Singapore merchants to accept payments from tourists through a wider pool of foreign payment networks and Singaporeans to pay through local apps in more countries.

Development of the SGQR+ switch, which will provide an additional connection between participating schemes rather than require merchants or payment providers to replace their existing arrangements, is already under way.

A limited roll-out in 2027 will connect an initial group of participating schemes and test live payment journeys before expanding in scope in 2028.

Another key enhancement is deep-linking. Already live in Lazada checkouts via the OCBC app, it seamlessly opens shoppers’ preferred payment app when they select PayNow when checking out on an e-commerce platform. This eliminates the need to screenshot or download QR codes and retrieve them in the payment app from their phone gallery.

Higher PayNow limits will also allow Singaporeans to make and receive larger government payments with instant confirmation. The enhancement will first be introduced in late 2027 with one government agency, which has not been identified, before being progressively rolled out to other agencies from 2028.

Singapore currently applies a $200,000 limit for PayNow, which constrains its use for some high-value payments, such as property down payment or full payments for cars, above this threshold.

Clearer and more consistent rules will also be developed to address payment disputes, refunds, fraud and scams that may arise from individuals’ PayNow transactions to merchants.

This could offer customers and merchants a more consistent dispute resolution experience, with clearer processes and potentially faster resolution in certain cases, particularly those involving technical issues.

Such safeguards will be introduced in stages over 2028 by the Singapore Payments Network (SPaN), which was set up in 2025 by MAS and ABS to oversee Singapore’s national and cross-border payment schemes.

MAS will bring together SPaN, Banking Computer Services and other key partners to innovate new payment capabilities for emerging use cases, including AI agent-initiated payments.

Industry participants, including ABS, banks and payment service providers, will also test ways to process very large numbers of frequent micro-payments more cheaply.

OCBC said it has already enabled PayNow deep-linking with platforms such as Lazada, Pinduoduo, AXS, Frasers Mall and AnyWheel, as well as government agencies like the CPF Board for a more seamless checkout experience.

UOB said it is working with industry partners to explore some of the capabilities envisioned under the plans to enhance PayNow Generation 2, including how deep-linking and account-to-account payments can be more seamlessly integrated into online shopping journeys.

data.title: NETS pilots ‘tap QR to pay’; new app features make payments easier for tourists
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Consumers can soon use smartphones to complete purchases at NETS payment points – without scanning a QR code.

This was among the enhancements to the Nets app announced on Nov 18.

Nets is the first to pilot the tap QR facility to pay via SGQR.

This feature enables consumers to make payments simply by tapping their near-field communication (NFC)-enabled smartphones at participating Nets SGQR points, without first opening the app.

It offers a convenient alternative to the existing scan-to-pay method.

This initiative, to run for two months will be piloted in phases, starting in Toa Payoh in December. There are plans for a nationwide roll-out if the pilot is successful.

Tapping to pay via QR will initially be available through the Nets app, with support for other participating banking apps and wallets expected over time.

Nets’ chief executive Lawrence Chan said: “As usage expands, our priority is to make QR payments more accessible for everyone, including visitors to Singapore, while advancing interoperability across the payments ecosystem.”

The other new features on the app will also benefit groups such as tourists, said the payments services group.

From now, those whose home-country payment apps are not linked to Singapore’s single, standardised QR code, or SGQR, can also use the local payment ecosystem through the Nets app.

Visitors from countries with established QR cross-border linkages with Singapore, such as China, India and Indonesia, can continue to pay directly through their local bank or wallet apps.

The other enhancements include a family wallet, through which users can use sub-wallets to support the spending needs of their dependants.

The primary user can set a spending limit and be notified of the transactions in their sub-wallets. THE BUSINESS TIMES

data.title: Dollar holds near 19-month high as data supports case for US rate hikes
data.description:
TOKYO – The dollar held steady near a 19-month high on Nov 18 as US economic data and comments from Federal Reserve officials lent support to the case for interest rate hikes.

The yen held its ground after Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Kazuo Ueda reiterated the need to tighten policy further. The Australian dollar fell to a 10-month low ahead of a key jobs report on Nov 19.

Data on Nov 17 showed US retail sales increased moderately in October, reinforcing expectations for a rate hike in December.

Attention turns to US housing starts data due later on Nov 18 and a series of Fed speakers, ahead of the Nov 19 release of minutes of the central bank’s meeting in October, when it held rates steady.

“Overall, the report reinforces our view that further interest rate hikes from the Fed are warranted in order to counter demand-pull inflation,” Henry Russell, a London-based economist for ANZ, said about the US sales data. “The strength of domestic demand in the US, in our view, warrants a decisive monetary policy response from the Fed.”

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose 0.06% to 103.67. It touched 103.78 overnight, its highest level since April 2, 2025. The euro was down 0.14% at US$1.0982, while the yen edged up 0.08% to 159.25 per dollar. Sterling lost 0.13% to US$1.3191.

In addition to a 0.2% rise in retail sales that matched expectations, import prices climbed 1.1% in October compared with expectations for a 0.7% increase.

More US data is expected with the Census Bureau due to report housing starts data for October. Analysts are projecting an increase to 1.245 million from 1.221 million in September, while building permits likely decreased.

New York Fed president John Williams is expected to speak again following comments on Nov 17 when he said the Fed will likely need to raise interest rates further to contend with inflation. Fed Board governor Michael Barr and Minneapolis Fed president Neel Kashkari are also expected to speak at separate events.

Traders are pricing in a 95.7% chance that the Fed will raise its key rate by 25 basis points (bps) in December, the CME FedWatch tool showed. The odds of a 50-bp increase have fallen to 4.3%, from 13.5% a month ago.

“All Fed speakers are saying that the Fed should raise rates in an incremental way,” said Tapas Strickland, chief market strategist at Moomoo ANZ, on a podcast. “The reduction in the probability of a supersized move has resulted in a bit more stability re-emerging in markets.”

Markets got a measure of relief after Nvidia reported after the bell that third-quarter revenue doubled and forecast higher-than-estimated sales for the fourth quarter, boosting shares in Asia

The next major test of sentiment will be the market debut of AI bellwether Anthropic on Nov 19.

Japanese data on Nov 18 showed exports rose to a record monthly value in October on strong semiconductor-related demand. Also in Tokyo, BOJ governor Ueda said the central bank should continue raising interest rates, while stressing the need to anchor underlying inflation around its 2% target.

The Australian dollar sank 0.18% versus the greenback to US$0.6719 and earlier touched US$0.6718, its lowest point since Jan 19. Nov 18 data showed a surprise jump in wages, but labour figures on Nov 19 are considered more crucial to determining if the central bank will need to hike rates again.

The New Zealand dollar slid 0.07% to US$0.5488, nearing its 19-month low hit on Nov 17. REUTERS

data.title: Bank of Japan governor says central bank should keep raising rates
data.description:
TOKYO - Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Nov 18 that the central bank should continue raising interest rates, while stressing the need to anchor underlying inflation around its 2% target.

Speaking in Parliament, Ueda said it was important to see underlying inflation anchored around 2% over time and conduct monetary policy appropriately to ensure that this could be achieved.

“Given that financial conditions are still accommodative, it would be appropriate to continue raising the policy rate and adjust the degree of monetary easing in line with developments in the economy, prices and financial conditions,” Ueda said.

The BOJ kept interest rates steady at 1.25% at its Oct 30 meeting but declared victory in its 14-year battle to hit its price target and stressed its policy had entered a new phase focused on avoiding an inflation overshoot, reinforcing its hawkish bias.

Ueda said the planned consumption tax cut on food would likely support economic growth by boosting households’ real purchasing power, though the size of the impact would depend on factors such as companies’ pricing behaviour and consumer sentiment.

Once the details of the measure are finalised, the central bank will assess its impact on underlying inflation and reflect that analysis in future policy decisions, he added.

Asked about the possibility of emergency bond-buying operations, Ueda said the BOJ would make a comprehensive assessment based on conditions at the time, including whether serious disruptions to market functioning had emerged and required a policy response.

He also cautioned against using such operations to contain long-term yields, saying the move could prove counterproductive if markets perceive the BOJ as helping finance government spending.

“In that case, long-term interest rates could become even more volatile,” he said. REUTERS

data.title: Nvidia delivers strong results as investors weigh post-Huang future​
data.description:
SAN FRANCISCO - Nvidia forecast quarterly revenue above Wall Street estimates on Nov 17, giving investors some relief after longtime leader Jensen Huang’s resignation plunged the chip firm into crisis.

Shares of the company rose nearly 4% in extended trading but remained down about 17% for the year through the Nov 17 close. The company is valued at roughly US$3.8 trillion (S$4.9 trillion).

“Our momentum is real,” interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress said, without addressing the leadership uncertainty. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track.”

With Huang gone, investors are looking for clues about Nvidia’s future, from billions of dollars invested in cloud providers, suppliers and AI startups to who will ultimately lead the world’s most valuable chipmaker.

The AI boom’s most prolific salesman resigned last week after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two Nvidia employees.

US intelligence agencies are trying to determine the extent of Alice Huang’s ties to China’s Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, according to two people familiar with the matter.

Huang’s exit ended three decades of founder-led control over Nvidia’s chip roadmap, customer deals and Washington ties, making execution a bigger risk than near-term AI demand, analysts say.

The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of US$130 billion, plus or minus 3%, above analysts’ average estimate of US$125.25 billion, according to LSEG data. Nvidia said the outlook assumes no data-center chip sales to China.

Adjusted gross margin is expected at 71% to 72%, compared with analysts’ estimate of 71.7%.

Finance chief Colette Kress is interim CEO, while the board considers internal and external candidates. A growing “Stand With Jensen” campaign has complicated the search, although the board is not considering Huang’s return, three people told Reuters on Nov 16. Huang said on Nov 17 he would be “honoured” to return if the board deemed it best.

Earlier on Nov 17, Nvidia’s board created a committee on national security and export controls, its first major governance move since Huang’s departure, as scrutiny grows over the chipmaker’s national security role.

Washington has also tightened licensing rules for chip shipments to South-east Asia and overseas data centers serving Chinese firms, while lawmakers prepare to question Huang, who had pushed for greater chip exports to China.

Investors were already uneasy about AI spending after Democrats’ midterm sweep fueled fears of tougher scrutiny and slower data-center expansion. They also want to know whether Nvidia’s next CEO will continue financing customers, a practice critics call circular.

The Nov 17 results offer a first read on Vera Rubin, Nvidia’s newest generation of AI processors and successor to Grace Blackwell. Nvidia said in August that Vera Rubin would account for about a fifth of data-center revenue in the October quarter and forecast 70% revenue growth in the next fiscal year.

Nvidia’s third-quarter revenue more than doubled to US$115.84 billion, beating analysts’ estimate of $109.11 billion. The company has topped Wall Street’s revenue expectations for 17 straight quarters.

Adjusted gross margin rose to 74.9% from 73.5% a year earlier, also beating analysts’ estimate of 74.1%, despite soaring memory prices and production ramps. REUTERS
